_help: A chip file. Everything the tooltips say comes from here, so write it in your own words.
Save the file and it reloads. Then open a source file and run 'Retro ASM: Switch chip'.
Only id, name and instructions are needed to start; add the rest as you go.
For full worked examples, look at tms9900.json, z80.json, 6502.json (C64) and bbc.json inside the extension's dialects folder.
name: __NAME__

syntax._help: How the source is laid out. Delete a line to get the usual default.

caseFormat._help: Which letter case each part is changed to when the file is saved (or Shift+Alt+U is pressed): upper, lower or keep (leave as typed). The words come from this file's instructions, directives and registers. Delete this section to use the defaults (instructions and registers upper, directives and labels kept).

lineUp._help: Where each part of a line starts when the code is lined up (Shift+Alt+L), counting from 0. A label always starts in column 0. commentGap is the fewest spaces kept before a comment. Delete this section to use 8, 16 and 32.

registerView._about: How the Registers panel reads operands. bareIs: what an operand with no # or brackets is ('number' as on the Z80, 'memory' as on the 6502). immediatePrefix: the mark in front of a plain number ('#' on the 6502, or leave it out). bits: how wide a register is (8 or 16). To show what a register holds, add "copy": {"to": 0, "from": 1} (operand numbers, counting from 0) to a load instruction, "copy": {"toReg": "A", "from": 0} when it always loads one register, "store": {"fromReg": "A", "to": 0} for a store, or "fixed": {"to": 0, "value": 0} for a clear.

registers.about: One line about what a register is on this chip.

operandForms.name: Memory at an address
operandForms.help: What this way of writing an operand means.

_help: ops says what each operand is: g = a register or memory place, i = a number, t = a label to jump to, r = a register.
explain is the sentence shown as 'This line:'. {1} and {2} stand for the first and second operand.
Add "local": true to short jumps, so the labels they go to are tucked inside their routine in the Outline.

directives._help: kind is one of: equ, data, text, space, include, import, export, origin, end, macro, endmacro, if, elif, else, endif, for, next, skipto, other. ops is [fewest, most] operands.

EQU.name: Equate
EQU.summary: Gives a name to a number.

ORG.name: Origin
ORG.summary: Says where in memory the following code goes.

DW.name: Words
DW.summary: Puts words (2 bytes each) into the program.

sprites._help: Shapes for the picture editor. Put a comment starting '@sprite 8x8' (or another shape name) above a block of DB lines to draw it. order: rows (one row after another), columns (8-row strips, down then across) or cells (8-row cells, across then down).

8x8.name: 8x8 character
8x8.about: 8 bytes, one a row, top row first.

snippets._help: Starter code: type the name (lower case) on an empty line, or run 'Retro ASM: Insert starter code'. ${1:NAME} is a spot to fill in (Tab moves on; the same number changes everywhere), $0 is where the cursor ends up, and a real $ is written \$ here.

routine.name: A routine
routine.about: A block of code you call, which comes back with RTS.

addresses._help: Hex address (no prefix) and what lives there. Shown when that address is hovered.
